approval.rationale: Design-only candidate in the approved-contract schema, not self-approval of this PR. Independent review, authorized merge, and separate A4.3 implementation authorization are required. This exact unchanged contract must exist in the implementation BASE. No same-PR redesign, historical Dataset exemption, or checker change may substitute for that authority.

identity.name: Multi-Source Dataset atomic publication v1
identity.purpose: Bound future publication of one fully prepared and privately verified immutable Multi-Source Dataset directory using true atomic no-replace publication. Cleanup is limited to current-invocation-owned uncommitted private staging. Existing Dataset, Canonical and Observation authorities and artifacts remain unchanged.

implementation_bindings.rationale: The sole os.rename occurrence is authorized only for Windows true atomic no-replace publication of the current invocation's verified owned staging to its exact previously absent immutable multi-source dataset ID destination. No generic rename, replacement, movement of existing final builds, or overwriting is authorized.

The sole shutil.rmtree occurrence may remove only the exact private staging directory exclusively created and still owned by this invocation before commit. It is never a caller-selected deletion API and cannot remove pre-existing staging, any final build, upstream artifacts, repository content or production data.

initiators: The future A4.3 Multi-Source Dataset materializer operating on one exact validated multi_source_dataset_id, explicit safe output_root and explicit built_at metadata
authority_boundary.mutation_owner: src/market_vault/multi_source/materialization.py owns only its invocation's private uncommitted staging and the absent-to-committed publication boundary of one exact final Multi-Source Dataset directory.
forbidden_bypass_layers: No generic filesystem mutation API, arbitrary caller-selected cleanup path, dynamic destructive dispatch, or indirect renamed call may expand these exact bindings.
No os.replace, path.replace, Path.replace, path.rename, Path.rename, shutil.move, os.remove, os.unlink, path.unlink, Path.unlink, os.rmdir, path.rmdir, Path.rmdir or delete-then-rename publication.
Never fall back to ordinary POSIX os.rename: an existing empty destination can be replaced. Unsupported no-replace semantics must fail closed.
No prospective_transition, new exemption, reuse of historical Dataset exemptions, checker weakening, or same-implementation-PR contract redesign.
No mutation of upstream Canonical, Observation, existing Dataset, Catalog, provider evidence, source evidence or production state; no provider acquisition, OpenD, CLI or UI route.

mutated_assets: Exactly one .<multi_source_dataset_id>.tmp-<random> staging directory acquired by exclusive creation under the explicit safe output root
The absent-to-committed boundary at <output_root>/<multi_source_dataset_id> through true same-filesystem atomic no-replace directory publication
excluded_assets: Every existing final directory, including corrupt, conflicting or partially damaged builds
Pre-existing staging, another invocation's staging, orphan crash residue, unrelated output-root children and the output root itself
Canonical artifacts, Observation artifacts, old Dataset artifacts, Catalog artifacts, source/provider evidence, repository content and production state

allowed_transitions.rationale: Only successful true atomic no-replace publication of the completely prepared, privately verified and still invocation-owned directory commits.
Destination-exists refusal is followed by strict read-only verification of the exact equivalent final Dataset, then cleanup only of this invocation's owned staging.
Preparation, verification, ownership/path drift, unsupported no-replace capability or corrupt/conflicting final fails closed. Ordinary cleanup may remove only still-proven owned uncommitted staging.

forbidden_transitions.rationale: Final publication is immutable; no reopening, repair, adoption or rollback to staging.
Idempotent success is terminal and cannot acquire ownership of the existing final.
A retry is a new invocation with new exclusive staging; never reuse or adopt residue.
A post-commit reader/caller failure must be reported without undoing durable publication or deleting the final directory.

commit_point.durable_authority: Successful true same-filesystem atomic NO-REPLACE directory publication of complete privately verified staging to the exact absent multi_source_dataset_id path. _SUCCESS inside staging is not the durable commit.
commit_point.success_authoritative_when: The entire immutable final directory is published without replacing any destination and the separate strict Multi-Source Dataset reader verifies its exact logical ID, matrix, all associations/evidence, specs, audit facts, output bytes and empty marker.

pre_commit: Before commit final remains absent unless another invocation published it; private staging including any _SUCCESS is non-authoritative.
A crash can leave staging residue; a future invocation never adopts, scans for automatic garbage collection, or deletes it.
During publication the primitive exposes the full directory or no publication; a partially visible final is forbidden.
post_commit: The final remains immutable even if the process crashes before returning a result.
No rollback deletion, repair, replacement, rewrite, quarantine or rename is authorized after commit; recovery is strict read/verify only.

restorable: Before commit, ordinary handled failures may clean only the exact directory exclusively created by this invocation after revalidating retained ownership and safe ancestry.
non_restorable: Post-commit rollback is unsupported; even subsequent verification failure cannot mutate final.
When ownership, object identity, ancestry or type cannot be proven, leave residue and report cleanup refusal; do not broaden deletion.
interruption_detection: A pre-existing selected staging path means collision, residue or another invocation: fail closed without adoption or removal.
Distinguish no-replace success, explicit destination-exists, unsupported capability and all other errors; existence or _SUCCESS alone never proves ownership or commit.

same_request_retry: A retry is a new invocation. If the exact final exists before staging, strictly verify it first; exact equivalent returns created_new_build=false without creating staging.
Path, built_at, file timestamps and directory order do not define logical equivalence or select a winner.
completed_retry: Return a strictly verified equivalent final without changing its files, metadata, marker or location.
conflicting_retry: Corrupt or conflicting final fails closed with no repair, replacement, deletion or quarantine.
After a publication race, apply exactly the same read-only equivalence rule and clean only this invocation's uncommitted staging.

lock_authority: The true atomic no-replace filesystem primitive is destination exclusion authority; final.exists() is only an optimization.
Exclusive staging creation plus an invocation-scoped object ownership record is cleanup authority; a pathname alone is not.
lock_scope: One owned staging directory and one exact final Dataset ID sibling under the explicit safe root; no global Catalog or production lock.
under_lock_revalidation: Retain exact staging path and filesystem-object identity, output root identity and intended final identity; revalidate before publication and cleanup.
Require safe output-root/staging/final ancestry, exact unchanged privately verified contents, same-filesystem placement and no path substitution.
concurrent_behavior: Windows uses exactly one os.rename(staging, final) in _rename_directory_no_replace_windows under Windows no-replace semantics; existing destination becomes an explicit internal destination-exists result.
Linux uses narrowly bounded native renameat2(..., RENAME_NOREPLACE). EEXIST or ENOTEMPTY becomes destination-exists.
Missing renameat2, EINVAL, ENOSYS, ENOTSUP or EOPNOTSUPP is unsupported and fails closed; all unexpected errors also fail closed.
Other platforms fail closed without a separately reviewed proven primitive. No ordinary POSIX rename, replace or delete-then-rename fallback.
A concurrent winner is never overwritten, removed or repaired. Strictly verify equivalence; return existing success or fail, cleaning only owned staging in either case.

identities: Exact multi_source_dataset_id and its normalized scope, logical schema/content, specs, implementations, completion, Canonical pins, A3 component/combined identities and complete Observation proof/audit identities
Exact output root, exclusively created staging filesystem object, invocation ownership and intended sibling final ID
Complete privately verified matrix, all association/evidence/spec artifacts, report, manifest and _SUCCESS before publication
drift_behavior: Fail closed on symlinks, junctions, Windows reparse points, path escape, unsafe output-root/staging/final ancestry, cross-filesystem publication or unverifiable type.
Inspect path components before traversal. Resolve-only containment is insufficient, including a reparse target that remains inside the root.
Ownership or path substitution prohibits publication and cleanup of the uncertain object. Never follow a link to mutate another location.
Final appearing concurrently is refused by the primitive and verified read-only; it never becomes cleanup-owned staging.

authoritative_evidence: Successful atomic no-replace publication and strict new-reader verification of the complete exact immutable Multi-Source Dataset
Strict read-only verification of an already existing exact equivalent final, returned idempotently without final mutation
non_success_evidence: In-memory orchestration alone, a staging path, partial file, or _SUCCESS without a complete verified final
An exists() precheck, cleanup completion, an unsupported primitive or corrupt/conflicting destination
integrity_binding: Directory name, reconstructed new Dataset ID, logical matrix/schema, all component and combined associations, complete Observation evidence, specs and implementation pins must agree.

Every output byte size/hash and canonical manifest/empty marker must pass the sole new reader including final second-pass content closure; build report and paths are not independent trust authorities.

invalidation_triggers.rationale: No UI plan or preview exists in A4 core; execution-time identity, ownership and path revalidation remains mandatory.

confirmation_invalidation.rationale: No user-data deletion or destructive confirmation UI is introduced.

execution_policy.rationale: Only the internal future A4.3 materializer may invoke these primitives; no CLI/UI dispatch is authorized.

lifecycle_unit: One complete immutable Multi-Source Dataset directory with matrix, association/evidence files, all spec artifacts, report, manifest and marker
partial_mutation: Partial visible final publication is forbidden; privately prepare and verify all files before one atomic same-filesystem no-replace publication.
Windows uses only its bound no-replace os.rename; Linux uses renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE); unsupported semantics fail closed.
rollback_expectation: Before commit, remove only invocation-owned uncommitted staging when safe cleanup is still provable.
After commit, no rollback mutation, even on reader failure; leave immutable final for independent recovery review.

retained_dependents: Every upstream Canonical/Observation artifact, old Dataset/Catalog artifact, source/provider evidence, unrelated output-root child, other staging and production state remains untouched.
refused_cases: Pre-existing staging, substituted objects, unsafe ancestry, cross-filesystem publication, unsupported primitive and corrupt/conflicting final
Deleting, rewriting, replacing, repairing, quarantining or moving any committed final
unsupported_cases: Catalog or provider acquisition/deletion, Canonical/Observation/old Dataset mutation, PIT mutation, source-evidence mutation or production cleanup
Orphan scanning/adoption, garbage collection, broad staging sweeps or recursive cleanup outside current owned staging
Permanent deletion, generic filesystem mutation and any additional destructive AST surface outside the two exact bindings

permanent_deletion.rationale: Owned pre-commit staging cleanup is an internal failure boundary, not a user-data deletion feature. No committed Multi-Source Dataset deletion is authorized.

implementation_tests: Inventory and exact-BASE PR gate require src/market_vault/multi_source/materialization.py:_rename_directory_no_replace_windows destructive_call os.rename expected_count=1.
Inventory and exact-BASE PR gate require src/market_vault/multi_source/materialization.py:_remove_tree destructive_call shutil.rmtree expected_count=1.
No additional destructive finding, prospective transition, exemption or checker modification; this exact unchanged merged BASE contract owns both surfaces.
Actual Windows no-replace refusal preserves existing final bytes, including an empty destination; the Windows helper is never used on POSIX.
Linux renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) refuses existing destination with EEXIST/ENOTEMPTY and preserves the winner.
Missing primitive, unsupported platform/filesystem, EINVAL/ENOSYS/ENOTSUP/EOPNOTSUPP, other errors and cross-filesystem paths fail closed without overwrite fallback.
Publication races never overwrite/delete/repair/move final; equivalent winner returns idempotently, corrupt/conflicting winner fails.
Handled pre-commit failure removes only current exclusively created staging and preserves unrelated root children and all source artifacts.
Pre-existing or substituted staging, other invocations and crash residue are never adopted, deleted or swept; uncertain ownership refuses cleanup.
Existing final before staging is strictly verified without staging creation; no final is ever repaired, replaced, rewritten or deleted.
Pre-commit residue/_SUCCESS alone is non-authoritative; publication is all-or-nothing; post-commit crash/verification failure never rolls back final.
Reject unsafe member syntax, symlinks, junctions, Windows reparse points including non-escaping ones, path escape, unsafe ancestry and unverifiable type.
Second-pass manifest/marker/output byte and root/inventory closure rejects same-path concurrent tampering before trusted result construction.
Canonical, Observation, old Dataset, Catalog, repository and production content stay untouched on success/failure/retry/race; every frozen prior identity vector remains unchanged.
